author: Ifmyante
text:
Expecting Supply or Demand to work, just because they're there, is
looking for serious trouble, and is contrary to everything I teach about
 trading!

Sure, PCP is a great place to look for a trade, but you need real PA to do so.

I think I warned you yesterday about assuming that engulfing into a gap is PA, which is exactly what you did here.

Also, on your M5 chart, your target seems arbitrarily drawn, and takes no account of the obvious left shoulders.

I know you know all these things. Just give yourself time to let them all sink in.

I feel you've lost a learning opportunity by asking me to show you what was wrong with your trades.

I'm happy to answer your questions, but you'd be far better off by including your own hypotheses in your posts

author: Ifmyante
text:
My post really wasn't intended to chastise you, so I'm sorry if it seemed so.

I've just been thinking an awful lot about the trader's mindset, and how it's probably more important than his knowledge base.

To prepare yourself for trading professionally, you must, from the very
beginning, train yourself to spot everything that stands in the way of
price, and increase your understanding of how it will affect price once
it gets there.

It will always be you, and only you, who presses the button on your
trades, and you'll have to be a master of critical thinking to do it
well

author: Ifmyante
text:
Okay, so I've just been invited to another RTM trading room via skype.

This happens quite often, and I'm glad to be included.

These trading rooms are run by their members, of course, and access is by invitation only.

If any of you would like access to any of these rooms, the way in is simple:

Make yourself known here in RTM, in your journal while you're learning,
and in the Trade Room thread once you're confident in your analysis.

If you fit with the group in personality and skill, you may very well get an invite.

Sure, you can all just group up with random members, but it may very
well end up being the blind leading the blind, getting everybody
confused on the wrong path.

The groups I've seen are doing great work already, and are quite organised, so I'd suggest earning an invite to one of them.

If you're already a respected trader here, beware of new groups inviting
 you, as they may be looking for a leader to show them the way.

The group should be as good a fit for you as you are for it. Then you'll have synergy

author: Rinehart
text:
PinkPanter wrote: the other BIG mistery is NEWS releases, who buys in that milisecond,
 so the price spike up directly into supply and reverses and goes in
other direction than big news pole? if they know that price will bounce
why they buy it??

PinkPanter, news releases works almost exactly the opposite way most
people imagine. The big spikes that happen right before and during a
news release are rarely caused by ITs dropping massive orders and then
reversing their orders with even more massive orders the other way.
What often happens is that some IT's (since ITs trade different time
frames too) remove their orders from the market. This causes a vacuum
of orderflow where price moves to find new equilibrium. When we are
talking about a spike to supply, there was more demand than supply once
IT pulled their orders. This allows the sharp move higher to strong
supply or an area with lots of retail buy stops (because IT takes
opposite of retail). Then price falls because of overwhelming supply.

author: Edge
text:
They know that many are seeking the next thing with trading. For years
 they used plain old TA strategies to teach the masses. This was
designed to create deep pools of liquidity in specific areas to fill
their own orders. Some have cottoned onto this, so in recent times they
have started campaigns focused on events over a specific time frame.
Think "trade the US election", Trade Brexit, Trade the German Election".
 Sure this has been around a while but the marketing campaigns
surrounding this 'macro' trading style have really stepped up. So they
are using these methods as well to get retailers thinking they are the
next Gordon Gekko. At the end of the day its all about getting the
retailer and smaller funds into positions to get their liquidity. This
will never change.

It is sick. Very true. Talking about front running and knowing where
clients order blocks are. The big institutions not only fill large
orders for clients etc, they have their own prop desks which front run.
Think of a LSK or Lovely UFL/LFL where we know there are orders
residing. When we get to it, they will often front run and issue new
orders in where the QM level is. These orders are added after the
initial order blocks are left behind from the original kink. This gives
us our QM. If they want extra they will FO and Diamond up to the very
last MPL of the true supply and demand. So quite often the QM is an
example of front running or adding fresh orders into a level

author: Atari
text:
Although our industry is full of manipulations by the ITs, I believe
we all should not focus our attention on the matter. It is beyond your
control currently and worrying and stressing about it would not make you
 a better trader. You all have been given an edge that basically tells
you where the ITs are trading (levels). As Edge pointed out, we have QM
 and DM, that in itself is how the ITs are trading and communicating
with each other. Don't get yourself boggle down with HFTs and wasting
your energy in the wrong area. Focus your energy on mastering RTM.
When you can master RTM, you know where the big guys are playing, when
they are manipulating, and where likely they will take price to next.
Once you have this down you just join them in their game without them
knowing and steal away orders from them. You can basically predict the
next move with high accuracy. That is the key. There are other older
RTM members prior to the launch of the new websites that have a equity
curve in a 70 degree angle and all he trades is the QM and DM. He does
not concern himself with HFTs and what else out there that is not
beneficial to his psychology and trading. All he does is focus his
energy on trading the QM and DM when it appears. We here at RTM have an
 edge like no one else out there. We have all the pieces of the puzzle
of the market. Consider yourself fortunate to have found RTM while 95%
of the retailers out there are still looking for the goose that lays the
 golden egg. Therefore, I highly recommend everyone to focus their
attention on becoming a master of RTM and don't get side tracked with
the things that you cannot control.
